item.title: Cornell case puts New York’s progressive image at odds with its rape laws
item.description:
A case alleging that a Cornell sophomore was sexually assaulted by seven fraternity members is drawing national attention. Spencer Platt/Getty Images Universities have been trying for years to cut back on the abuses among fraternities, with limited resources and limited success. A new lawsuit , filed by a former Cornell University student in September 2026, is now rattling higher education and drawing national attention . The person, identified as Jane Doe, has alleged that seven Chi Phi fraternity members drugged and gang-raped her at an on-campus fraternity house when she was a sophomore in 2024. Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten declined to pursue criminal charges against the fraternity members in 2024. item.title: Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as German chancellor visits Ukraine in show of support
item.description:
Attack shortly after Friedrich Merz arrived on unannounced visit intended to underline Germany’s backing Russia has struck another major bridge in Kyiv as the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, arrived in the capital in a show of support for Ukraine. A Russian drone hit Kyiv’s key Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River, marking the fourth consecutive day that Russia has targeted bridges used by tens of thousands of residents commuting between the city’s two banks. Video footage showed cars driving across the bridge as the drone plunged into the roadway and exploded in a burst of fire. Two people were injured in the strike, said Kyiv’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko. item.title: France to shutter up to 500 schools as more student protests called
item.description:
Anti-riot police officers face protesting students carrying out blockading action outside the secondary school Le Corbusier, in Aubervilliers, northern Paris on October 1, 2026. —Lou Benoist—AFP/Getty Images High schools across France have closed, thousands of teenagers have been arrested, and hundreds of people have suffered injuries as unrest over conditions in the lycée system has spread and erupted into violence in recent days. Roughly 3,000 people have been arrested since the protests began nearly two weeks ago outside of Paris, with nearly 2,000 being detained on Thursday alone, the French interior ministry announced. item.title: Iran says no military solution to war as peace talks with US stall
item.description:
The US dispatched another aircraft carrier and thousands more troops to the Middle East , signaling a potential escalation in the Iran war. US President Donald Trump said in a recent interview that a resumption of military strikes was “ possible ,” after last month rejecting an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran, meanwhile, is preparing its own response to any American attacks , Reuters reported. Iran seems “determined not to respond symbolically to a symbolic move and instead to escalate in the ⁠hope of reestablishing deterrence,” one expert said. Oil surged 4% on the news : Crude flows out of the Gulf last month were almost back to prewar levels, but analysts cautioned that any recovery in overall supply was fragile. — Prashant Rao

item.title: Police investigating Flydubai co-pilot’s Australia ties
item.description:
Oman had banned the FlyDubai co-pilot accused of stabbing his captain in an attempted hijacking from flying over concerns that he had adopted “radical ideological views,” according to a new report. Despite the ban, FlyDubai hired the Omani national, allowing him to fly the route between the United Arab Emirates and Israel, The Wall Street Journal reported. The Journal could not determine whether Oman had shared its concerns about the suspected terrorist with other airlines or countries Aviation-security analysts told The Journal that the attack exposed a major security failure. Even if a screening lapse allowed a weapon through, they said, a motivated assailant should have been stopped before reaching the airport. item.title: Ethiopian rebel forces withdraw from Tigray regional capital
item.description:
Troops loyal to Ethiopia's federal government were patrolling the streets of Mekelle on Sunday, a day after the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) withdrew its forces from the northern city. The government advance came as Ethiopia's regional rivals including Eritrea and Sudan met in the Egyptian coastal city of El-Alamein, calling for regional disputes to be settled through "peaceful means".

item.description:
A section of the particle accelerator housed at CERN. AP Photo/Baz Ratner While scientists are known for their dedication to their research, crawling on the floor to avoid electrocution for the sake of a measurement seems a little excessive. But this is what British physicist John Cockcroft and Irish physicist Ernest T.S. Walton had to do in the early 1930s while studying the structure of atomic nuclei. Luckily, their efforts led to their receiving the Nobel Prize in 1951 . The Irish physicist Ernest Walton. The Nobel Foundation , CC BY In the early 1930s, scientists were just beginning to discover the extraordinary world hidden inside the atom , which is made up of a dense center, called the nucleus, with electrons orbiting around it. item.title: Bosnian Serb nationalist Dodik declares party victory in Bosnia election
item.description:
Staunchly pro-Russia politician has dominated campaign and inflamed divisions despite not appearing on ballot Bosnian Serb nationalist politician Milorad Dodik has declared victory for his party in an election in Bosnia shaped by economic pressures, the prospect of the Balkan nation joining the European Union and ethnic tensions that have divided the country since its brutal 1992-95 war. Dodik is a staunchly pro-Russia politician who, despite not appearing on the ballot, has dominated the campaign and inflamed divisions with separatist rhetoric that has sparked fears of renewed instability in Bosnia.
